docs.title: Flow Metrics & Pipeline Benchmarking
docs.text: As pipeline topologies grow in complexity, diagnosing latency spikes, camera frame drops, or throughput degradation across multiple processes can become challenging. Pipeline Creator integrates dedicated diagnostics and benchmark tools designed to provide complete observability over data transmission, queue occupancy, and execution performance without degrading user interface responsiveness.

docs.title: Flow Metrics Viewer
docs.text:
The Flow Metrics Viewer serves as an application-wide diagnostics and process manager. It provides a live, centralized overview of all instantiated modules, background worker processes, and connection links.

By continuously observing message frequencies, callback execution latencies, and queue fill levels across the graph, it allows operators to immediately pinpoint processing bottlenecks. Because telemetry relies on non-intrusive timestamp sampling and shared memory counters, the viewer runs with minimal footprint and can remain open during live production or data acquisition without degrading framerates.

Open it from the top menu bar via Tools → Flow Metrics.

docs.title: Global Resource Banner
docs.text:
The top bar displays live aggregate performance counters across the entire application:

  • UI FPS: Rendering framerate of the DearPyGui interface.
  • CPU %: Total normalized CPU consumption (0–100% across all CPU cores) combining the main UI process and all worker processes.
  • RAM MB: Total Resident Set Size (RSS) memory footprint in megabytes.
  • Modules: Total number of active module instances instantiated on the canvas.
  • Active Links: Total number of active wire connections between modules.
  • Worker Processes: Number of background worker processes spawned and running.

docs.title: Controls & Options
docs.text:
• Refresh (s): Adjust the telemetry polling interval between 0.1s and 2.0s (default: 0.5s).
  • Instrument input_cb: Checkbox to toggle lightweight timing probes on module callbacks. When enabled, it calculates incoming message frequencies (Hz) and execution duration (ms).
  • Export Snapshot (JSON): Saves a complete timestamped diagnostic report containing all module metrics, queue fill levels, and system stats to logs/benchmarks/flow_metrics_<timestamp>.json.

docs.title: Flow States & Visual Legend
docs.text:
Each row in the table is color-coded to immediately identify pipeline health and bottlenecks:

State Color Meaning READY / FLOWING Green Normal operation. The module is responsive, queues are healthy, and downstream consumers accept data. BUSY / QUEUE FILL Yellow High load. The worker is computing or the input queue is more than 50% full. WAITING / SATURATED Red Congestion / Bottleneck. A downstream consumer is blocking (HOLD), the input queue is full, or the worker has stopped. UI-THREAD / STANDBY Cyan Lightweight module executing directly on the main UI thread without a background worker process.

docs.title: Metrics Table Columns
docs.text: Column Description UUID Shortened unique identifier of the module instance. Module Label (Class) User-defined label of the node followed by its underlying Python class name. Flow State Live status indicator (READY, BUSY, WAITING (HOLD), UI-THREAD, IDLE). Links Out Number of outgoing connections. Displays a (HOLD) warning if downstream backpressure is blocking transmission. In Rate (Hz) Instantaneous incoming message rate calculated over a 2.5-second sliding window. input_cb (ms) Callback execution latency, showing the mean and 95th percentile (mean / P95 ms). Worker Status Process state and operating system PID (Running (PID: ...), Stopped, or UI-Thread). In Queue Current backlog of items versus total capacity (current / max, e.g. 2 / 10). Drop Policy Active queue overflow policy: drop_new (discard incoming), drop_oldest (latest wins), or block. Telemetry / Drops Cumulative call count, dropped frame counter, and custom module telemetry metrics.

docs.title: Node Editor In-Canvas Profiling
docs.text:
In addition to the global Flow Metrics Viewer, the Node Editor includes an embedded profiling tool that provides immediate visual feedback directly on the canvas. When enabled, it reveals live pipeline activity, pulses active data streams, and highlights where queues or connections are saturated.

Activate it in the Node Editor menu bar by checking the Profiling checkbox (1).

docs.title: Real-Time Flow & Heartbeat
docs.text: Once profiling mode is active, active nodes and connection wires pulse dynamically as data packets travel through the graph. This visual "heartbeat" makes it easy to distinguish between flowing pipelines, idle branches, and congested links at a glance. Blocked/Saturated modules (1-4) are colored in red.

docs.title: Node Quick Telemetry Popup
docs.text:
Right-clicking any node while in profiling mode displays a real-time status summary for that specific module:

This quick popup shows:

  • Instant Processing Times: Mean execution time of input_cb and processing frequency (Hz).
  • Targeted Output Inspection: Observe latency and throughput metrics for individual output terminals or across the module as a whole.
  • Queue Status: Instantaneous view of input queue fill levels and backpressure state.

docs.title: Full Telemetry Reports
docs.text:
Clicking View Full Report from the right-click popup opens a dedicated, floating performance report window for that node:

  • Interactive Multi-Axis Live Plot: Select which metrics to visualize simultaneously (rates in Hz, callback turnaround in ms, memory RSS/peak MB, queue fill percentage) across primary and secondary right Y-axes with interactive pan, wheel zoom, and cursor annotations.
  • Detailed Summary Table: Access comprehensive percentiles (mean, P95, max), execution latencies, invocation counts, memory allocation, and queue drop counts.
  • Per-Port Routing Table: Inspect individual output port rates, turnaround times, and downstream receiver availability status (OK vs HOLD).
  • Telemetry Export: Export the live telemetry session to CSV or JSON for post-run analysis.

Simultaneous Multi-Module Diagnostics & Stress Testing

You can open multiple telemetry report windows simultaneously across different nodes in your pipeline. By comparing live metrics side-by-side during runtime, you can observe exact inter-module interactions and precisely determine where, when, and how bottlenecks form.

This capability is particularly valuable when performing benchmarks or stress-testing custom nodes under sustained high-frequency loads. For dedicated stress test and synthetic workload generators, see Module Stress Testing & Benchmark Suite.

docs.title: In-Flow Propagation Tester (Speedometer Node)
docs.text:
For an ultra-lightweight way to monitor pipeline speed and latency without opening separate report windows, you can insert Propagation Tester nodes directly onto the canvas.

The Propagation Tester acts as an inline "speedometer gauge" that connects between any two points in the graph to measure the precise transit duration (Delta-t) of data packets across a sub-graph, pipeline hop, or module chain.

Add it via the canvas right-click context menu: Right Click Canvas → Add Node → Propagation Tester.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The node provides two specialized input pins:

  • Start (A): Connect to the output of the upstream sender (e.g. Module A). The timestamp is captured immediately as data leaves Module A.
  • Stop (B): Connect to the output of the downstream receiver or final processing node (e.g. Module B). The timestamp is captured upon completion, computing the elapsed propagation duration (Delta-t).

Because both pins act as transparent observation probes with zero backpressure (is_ready() permanently True), the Propagation Tester does not alter or delay the measured pipeline.

docs.title: Readouts & Metrics
docs.text:
The node body updates live directly on the canvas:

  • Instantaneous & Average Delta-t: Digital readout formatted with microsecond precision (mean, last, P95, min, max, std).
  • Inflow & Outflow Rates: Instantaneous frequencies (Hz) measured at Pin A and Pin B.
  • Packet Counters & Drops: Monitored count of matched pulses, unmatched events, and dropped frames.
  • Detailed Tooltip: Hovering over the node displays a complete latency breakdown and variance statistics.
  • Reset Button: Clears the sliding history window and counter registers at any moment during acquisition.

docs.title: Module Stress Testing & Benchmark Suite
docs.text:
To help developers stress-test module stability, queue overflow behavior, and throughput boundaries, and to help users benchmark their hardware capabilities when running demanding pipelines, Pipeline Creator includes a dedicated suite of synthetic Benchmark modules located in modules/benchmark/.

These tools allow you to generate variable, high-rate streams across all major IOTypes, as well as mock processing sinks capable of executing parameterized CPU or GPU workloads.

docs.title: Dual-Role Testing Architecture
docs.text:
The benchmark tools serve two primary operational roles:

  1. Producer Testing (Stress-testing your module's inputs):

Wire a benchmark producer directly into your custom module. You can configure payload sizes (e.g. 720p/1080p/4K frames, sample lengths from 16 to 100,000+ points, vector densities up to 65,536 elements) and stream emission rates (controlled 1–1000 Hz or uncapped CPU throughput).

This allows you to: - Identify the exact saturation point and maximum throughput of your module. - Verify that your queue drop_policy (drop_oldest, drop_new, block) triggers correctly under sustained overload. - Confirm that your module safely handles diverse data formats (e.g. 8-bit, 12-bit HDR, 16-bit HDR, masks, and accessory tuples).

  1. Sink Testing (Stress-testing your module's outputs):

Wire your custom module's outputs into a benchmark processor sink. The mock processor consumes incoming data while applying configurable processing workloads—from zero-compute pass-through (measuring pure IPC serialization latency) up to intensive CPU matrix burns or GPU acceleration.

This allows you to:

  • Observe how downstream backpressure (HOLD) impacts your upstream worker processes.

  • Measure at what processing delay downstream queues begin to fill and drop items.

  • End-to-End Hardware Benchmarking:

Connect benchmark producers and processor sinks together in various topologies (linear chains, fan-out branches, circular feedback loops) to evaluate your machine's CPU core scaling, OpenCL GPU compute, RAM bandwidth, and shared memory IPC limits.

docs.title: Available Benchmark Modules
docs.text:
The suite comprises specialized generator and consumer modules:

Module Role Supported IOTypes Key Capabilities Video Benchmark (video_benchmark_win.py) Producer FRAME, FRAME12, FRAME16, MASK, FRAME_MASK_PAIR Zero-allocation synthetic camera generator. Configurable resolutions (up to 4K), 8/12/16-bit depths, color spaces, noise patterns, and rates up to 500+ FPS or uncapped. Image Processor Benchmark (image_processor_benchmark_win.py) Processor / Sink FRAME, FRAME12, FRAME16, MASK, FRAME_MASK_PAIR, ANY Multiprocessing worker stress-tester. Features configurable algorithms (Pass-Through, Invert, Blur, Sobel, Canny, Bilateral, CPU matrix burn) with CPU vs OpenCL GPU hardware acceleration. Sample Benchmark (sample_benchmark_win.py) Producer SAMPLE, NUMBER, DATALIST High-frequency numerical sample generator. Pre-rendered waveforms (Sine, Chirp, Square, Noise, Random Walk), 16 to 100,000+ points, controlled 1–1000 Hz or uncapped. Sample Processor Benchmark (sample_processor_benchmark_win.py) Processor / Sink SAMPLE, NUMBER, DATALIST, ANY Multiprocessing numerical processing sink. Configurable simulated compute delay, queue capacity, and mathematical transformations. Vector Benchmark (vector_benchmark_win.py) Producer VECTORS, SAMPLE High-density vector field generator. Emits angular distributions (Spotlight, Bimodal, Pendulum, Vortex) with 16 to 65,536+ vectors per frame, burst mode, and batch mode. CMD Benchmark (cmd_benchmark_win.py) Producer / Tester CMD_DICT, TRIGGER, NUMBER, TEXT Command and control packet generator. Tests latency, response turnaround, and command sequencing. Hardware Simulator (hardware_simulator_win.py) Simulator / Sink TRIGGER, TEXT, ANY Simulates physical hardware device delays, communication timeouts, and intermittent failures for robust error-handling validation.

docs.title: Tutorial Manager Guide
docs.text: When working with complex pipelines the interface can quickly become intimidating for new operators. The Tutorial Manager is a visual utility designed to simplify this complexity. It allows you to record and replay step-by-step interactive tutorials that guide operators through a pipeline's interface by dimming the entire screen, drawing a high-contrast orange border around the active control widget, and displaying a floating instruction card featuring a helpful mascot.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• 🎥 Live Recording: Record actions on sliders, buttons, inputs, menus, and combos in real time.
  • 👁️ Observation Points: Record static highlight boxes to focus the user's attention on non-interactive elements (e.g., checking a plot or status indicator).
  • 🔆 High-Contrast Focus: Dims the rest of the screen and draws a glowing border around the active widget.
  • 🦖 Customizable Mascot: Displays instructions next to the active item accompanied by a mascot. By default, it uses Polypy, but you can configure a custom mascot/icon by placing your image files under ressources/tutorial_assets/.
  • 💾 Portable JSON Format: Tutorials are stored as portable JSON files in the config/tutorials/ directory, allowing them to be shared across setups.
  • 🛠️ Programmatic Workflow Enforcement: Developer modules can block actions in specific privilege modes (such as "user" mode) if a prerequisite is not met, and automatically trigger an overlay reminder highlighting the exact widget the user must interact with.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text:
Creating a tutorial is fully automated: you simply start the recording, interact with the UI elements in the sequence you want to demonstrate, and then write the custom instructions that should appear on screen for each step.

  1. Open the Tutorial Manager.
  2. Click the Record button.
  3. Left-Click any interactive widget (buttons, sliders, inputs) to record an Interact step.
  4. Middle-Click any static element (titles, charts, status texts, window) to record an Observe step.
  5. For each step:
  6. Customize the instructions by editing the text field next to the step.
  7. Check or uncheck Dim to toggle whether the screen should dim during this step.
  8. Click the Run button to test that specific step.
  9. Click the X button to delete a step.

To run a tutorial:

  1. Open the Tutorial Manager.
  2. Click the Load button and select a tutorial JSON file.
  3. Click Play (or Stop Playback to cancel).
  4. A floating instruction HUD will appear on screen:
  5. For Interact steps: perform the highlighted action (e.g., clicking the button) to automatically advance to the next step, or click the Next (→) button on the HUD.
  6. For Observe steps: hover your mouse cursor over the highlighted element to automatically advance, or click the Next (→) button on the HUD.
  7. Click the Prev (←) button on the HUD to go back a step.
  8. Click Close or Stop Playback at any time to exit the tutorial.

During playback, the Tutorial Manager includes an integrated task validation system that monitors user actions in real time. When a step highlights a widget (such as a button or slider), the manager detects when the user performs the required interaction on that widget and automatically validates the task to advance to the next step.

docs.title: Module-Specific Tutorials
docs.text:
Pipeline Creator allows you to link tutorials directly to custom modules:

  • Place a file named tutorial.json in the same directory as your module's Python file (e.g., modules/my_module/tutorial.json).
  • The Node Editor automatically detects this file at startup.
  • In the Node Editor canvas, right-click on the module's node to open its context menu.
  • A Show Tutorial button will automatically appear at the top of the context menu.
  • Clicking Show Tutorial will immediately load and play that module's specific tutorial.

Dimmed vs. Non-Dimmed View

You can also see the difference between a Dimmed and Non-Dimmed step.

docs.title: Lineplot Module
docs.text: The Lineplot module is an interactive 2D data visualization window designed to display, inspect, and analyze continuous time-series or XY curve signals in real time.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Multi-Series Rendering: Plot and manage multiple overlaid curves with customized labels, distinct UUID tracking, and legends.
  • Interactive Cursor Annotation: Dynamically detects and inspects the closest data point on mouse hover, displaying its index, X coordinate, and Y coordinate.
  • Vertical Reference Line: Add an interactive draggable vertical line (Drag Line) for thresholding or time synchronization, controllable manually or programmatically.
  • Signal Smoothing: Built-in moving average filter (rolling window convolution) with a configurable window size ($1$ to $50$) to filter out noise on the fly.
  • Logarithmic Scaling: Switch between linear and logarithmic X-axis scales (Log X).
  • Autoscale / Autofit: Automatic axis scaling on data updates to keep series in view.
  • TSV Clipboard Export: One-click export of all plotted series into Tab-Separated Values (TSV) directly to the system clipboard for immediate pasting into Excel, Prism, or Python.
  • Downstream Plot Streaming: Broadcast current plot data, axis limits, and configuration via the CMD output (Send Plot).

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Supported Payload Formats & Actions IOTypes.SAMPLE / IOTypes.ROI_SAMPLE Dictionary containing x, y, name, uuid, and action ("select", "unselect", "delete", "rename", "clear"). IOTypes.CMD_DICT Command dictionary supporting actions: "position" (moves drag line), "add serie", "remove serie", "update serie name", "clear". IOTypes.DATALIST Numerical list or coordinate arrays (x, y) for legacy streaming.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Name Type Description Datalist IOTypes.DATALIST Emits data as a list of points. CMD IOTypes.CMD_DICT Emits structured plot packets with action: "plot_data", series list, title, labels, and axis limits.

docs.title: UI Controls
docs.text:
• Anotation (Checkbox): Enables hovering tooltips showing the nearest point's Index, X, and Y.
  • Drag Line (Checkbox): Toggles the interactive vertical cursor line.
  • Autoscale (Checkbox): Automatically fits X and Y axes when new data is received.
  • Smooth (Checkbox) & Win (Slider): Toggles moving average smoothing and sets the convolution window width ($1-50$).
  • Log X (Checkbox): Toggles logarithmic scaling on the horizontal axis.
  • Export TSV (Button): Copies all displayed series in column format (X, Series1, Series2...) to the clipboard.
  • Send Plot (Button): Packages the current graph state and transmits it to connected modules via CMD.
  • Clear Plot (Button): Removes all series and annotations from the canvas.

docs.title: Sample Container Module
docs.text: The Sample Container module is a centralized repository and manager for datasets (SAMPLE format). It allows storing, previewing, reordering, filtering, importing, and exporting multiple data series before streaming them to downstream visualization or analysis modules (such as Lineplot, Boxplot, or data processors).

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Sample Registry & List: Displays all loaded samples with individual toggles, names, and mini plot preview tooltips.
  • Interactive Drag-and-Drop Reordering: Easily reorder stored samples using drag handles to adjust their display and export sequence.
  • Mini-Plot Tooltip: Hovering over any sample's checkbox renders a thumbnail graph of the signal curve for quick visual inspection.
  • Duplicate Management:
  • override: Overwrites existing sample data when a sample with the same name is ingested.
  • append: Automatically appends a numeric suffix (e.g. Sample_1, Sample_2) to preserve both entries.
  • Batch Actions: One-click Select all, Deselect all, and Clear samples operations.
  • Flexible CSV Export:
  • X Axis Reference Modes:
    • index: Exports uniform integer indexing ($0, 1, 2\dots$) as the primary X axis.
    • individual: Generates separate paired columns (Name_X, Name_Y) for each selected sample.
    • Sample Reference: Uses a specific sample's X array as the shared timebase for all exported columns.
  • Export selected samples via dialog or auto-save headlessly.
  • Robust CSV Import: Automatically detects single X or multi-column paired (_X/_Y) spreadsheet layouts and registers samples into the container.
  • Reactive Event Streaming: Emits atomic events (action: "select", "unselect", "rename") whenever sample selection or naming changes.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text: Input Type Description IOTypes.SAMPLE Ingests sample data (x, y, name, action). IOTypes.FOLDER_PATH Configures the default working folder for CSV import and export. IOTypes.TRIGGER Triggers automated CSV export when receiving "save" or trigger pulse. IOTypes.CMD_DICT Command dictionary supporting actions like {"export": True}.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: Output Name Type Description Data IOTypes.SAMPLE Emits active sample data payloads with action tags ("select", "unselect", "rename").

docs.title: UI Controls
docs.text:
• Import/export (Collapsing Header):
  • X axis reference (Dropdown): Selects the reference mode (index, individual, or a specific sample).
  • Import CSV (Button): Opens file explorer to import series from a CSV file.
  • Export CSV (Button): Opens file explorer to save selected samples into a CSV spreadsheet.
  • Duplicate (Dropdown): Selects conflict resolution strategy (override vs append).
  • Clear samples (Button): Clears all samples from memory and sends unselect signals.
  • Select all / Deselect all (Buttons): Toggles selection state for all items simultaneously.
  • Sample List Items:
  • Drag Handle (☰): Drag to reorder sample position in the list.
  • Checkbox & Tooltip: Toggles sample activation (emits select / unselect) and displays mini-plot preview on hover.
  • Delete Button (🗑): Removes the individual sample.
  • Name Input: Rename the sample inline (emits rename update to connected nodes).
